subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should the fix preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism and target ACPX/Claude launch readiness, or should OpenClaw add an explicit concurrency gate for rapid ACPX/Claude spawns?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally allow different ACP sessions to run in parallel, so automation should not serialize that path without a maintainer decision and current live proof.

options.title: Validate, then preserve parallelism
options.body: Run the live two-spawn ACPX/Claude smoke and fix the confirmed launch/readiness failure while keeping different child sessions parallel by default.

options.title: Add an explicit concurrency gate
options.body: If live proof shows the backend cannot safely launch distinct Claude ACP sessions concurrently, add a documented and tested ACPX/Claude gate instead of relying on accidental timing.

options.title: Close after live non-repro
options.body: If a current live two-spawn smoke cannot reproduce the failure and logs show both children launch cleanly, close this issue with that proof.

recommendation.title: Validate, then preserve parallelism
recommendation.body: Run the live two-spawn ACPX/Claude smoke and fix the confirmed launch/readiness failure while keeping different child sessions parallel by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent adjacent ACP contract review context and can help decide whether empty/no-output ACP behavior is a runtime contract or a launch bug.
